en.title: Minimum and Maximum Endpoint Cost of Splitting into Exactly p Segments
en.description:
Split the whole array into exactly p non-empty contiguous segments. The cost of a segment is its first element plus its last element; a single-element segment counts that element twice. Output the minimum and the maximum total cost, in that order. The source's second example had them reversed; this site corrects it to 8 12.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n p; the second line contains the costs. The source gave no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, 1≤p≤n, costs 1..10^9.
en.output: Output the minimum cost and the maximum cost, separated by a space.
hints: Every split includes the cost of the first and last elements, and each cut between i and i+1 adds a[i]+a[i+1]; choose the smallest or the largest p−1 adjacent sums.
